cells.tense: The close is happening now, and your attention is still on it.
cells.act: commit to the long build and do today's part
cells.ask: With the ending already decided, give an hour to the physical sorting — one drawer or shelf — until what stays and what goes is plain, and stop at the hour.
cells.core:
You can tell what still belongs from what has finished, and you do it with your own eyes rather than a rule. Where a chapter is closing, you keep looking until the line is clear, and then you act on it. Nothing drags because the deciding got done.

That same care can be put down for a moment. With the ending already decided, give an hour to the physical sorting — what stays, what goes — and leave the rest of the work where you found it. The closing gets its due, and you find out whether the deciding is finished or whether it keeps finding new rooms. Either way you'll have something in your hands, not another evening of weighing.

cells.verb: honing, through careful attention, what matters from what does not

cells.tense: You will have run the next ending through your mind before it has happened.
cells.act: do the next piece of it in front of the person it is for
cells.ask: Take the next part of the clearing and do it where the person it's for can see you — no announcement, no assembling them to watch.
cells.core:
You will have mapped the next ending in your head before it is here — what goes, what stays, who will mind, what it will cost. The refining is honest and it has a price: the ending arrives already rehearsed, so there's nothing left to feel when it comes. What was handed over quietly starts to feel like a debt you're tracking instead.

The counterweight is to let the handing over be visible. Do the next part of the clearing in front of the person it is actually for — no explanation, no gathering anyone to watch. If they say something, take it. If they don't, that's information too, not a verdict. The ending still ends; you just stop doing it alone, and find out whether the hiding was about you or about them.

cells.tense: You were standing at a chapter that had already closed behind you.
cells.act: let the exchange with someone run both ways
cells.ask: Put into words the part you played in this ending, then take whatever comes back without a tally.
cells.core:
You were standing at a door that had already closed behind you, still working out how to leave the room. What's finished has finished, but the refining keeps going: turning it over, checking the seam, postponing the actual goodbye. Attention is steady. Arrival isn't — you're two steps behind where the chapter ended.

The way back opens through exchange, not effort. Put into words the part you played in this ending, and then take whatever someone hands back, without a tally. Not a reckoning — one give, one receive, so the account runs both ways. Fairness returns when it's spoken, not when it's finally calculated right. The door was going to stay shut either way; this just puts you on the other side of it.

cells.tense: The ending is being done well, and it is being done without you counting.
cells.act: walk through the thing you built and touch nothing
cells.ask: Walk through what this ending already cleared — the corner, the shelf, the habit dropped — and touch nothing while you're there.
cells.core:
The clearing is happening, and the one doing it would say it's circumstance. What has ended is ending on time, the details are being handled, and the hand in it is invisible — mostly to you. You look at what's been cleared and call it luck or the natural order, and the person who did the ending is you. What you finished is standing there, uncredited by the one who made it.

Before reaching for what's next, walk through one finished piece. Take a thing this ending actually completed — a room emptied, a habit stopped, a tie let go — and go past it, touching nothing. No audit of what's still undone, no next task. Standing in what you cleared is how your name gets put back on it. The ending was yours; the staying with it should be too.

attempts.check: The record supports the shape of honing, but not that a sacrifice has actually been made or is being carried alone — 'what was given quietly' is my read, not a fact, and the person may rightly say nothing was sacrificed, the ending is simply slow. The ask survives being wrong: even if the giving was not a sacrifice, showing the next piece to the person it is for still returns something to the giver. The sentence that serves me rather than them is the one that flatters the private work into a virtue; the Too Much cell names the snag instead. The Transformation seat does not let me claim the ending has happened — every cell says what is closing, never who or how long ago.
